name: app.R
content:
###################################################################################
# Shiny app: The Text-Annotation Performance of LLMs Varies Across Levels of Task Complexity
#
# Interactive companion to the manuscript. The figures use the same data,
# variable labels, colours, reference lines and statistics as the article
# figures produced by 00_MASTER_analysis.R.
#
# Structure of the script
# 1. Packages
# 2. Configuration
# 3. Theme and helper functions
# 4. Data import and preparation
# 5. User interface (UI)
# 6. Server
#
# Principle: every plotOutput/uiOutput in the UI shows what the server creates
# as output$<id>. The selectInput menus pass the selection to the server as
# input$<id>; the server recomputes the affected outputs automatically.
###################################################################################


#############################################################
# 1. Packages
#############################################################

# Kept to a minimum: in the browser version (Shinylive) every package is
# downloaded by the visitor, so haven, tidyr and stringr are not used.
library(shiny)      # Shiny app
library(bslib)      # layout and design
library(dplyr)      # data preparation
library(ggplot2)    # figures
library(patchwork)  # combine ggplots


#############################################################
# 2. Configuration
#############################################################

# Data files, relative to the app folder. The two .rds files besides
# icr_list1.rds are plain copies of overview_human_icr.sav and exsvy_public.sav
# (SPSS labels removed), written by 03_export_shinylive.R.
DATA_DIR       <- "."
FILE_ICR       <- "icr_list1.rds"           # LLM-human reliability (see README_new.md)
FILE_HUMAN_ICR <- "overview_human_icr.rds"  # human-human reliability per variable
FILE_EXPERT    <- "exsvy_public.rds"        # public expert survey (no identifying columns)

N_ITEMS_EXPECTED <- 17
EXCLUDED_LEVELS  <- c("JUST_REF", "POS_REF")

# Reference lines, as in the article
ALPHA_REF <- 0.6   # Krippendorff's alpha
AGREE_REF <- 80    # percentage agreement (0-100)

PLOT_HEIGHT <- "520px"


#############################################################
# 3. Theme and helper functions
#############################################################

# theme_pnas(): on-screen version of the article's figure style
# (classic axes, black text, no legend). Font sizes are larger than the
# 6-8 pt print sizes because the figures are read on screen.
theme_pnas <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(size = base_size, color = "black"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(2, "mm"),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# App design (navigation bar, colours, fonts); theme_pnas() only styles the plots
app_theme <- bs_theme(
  version = 5,
  bootswatch = "litera",
  primary = "#34638B"
)

# Same helpers as in 00_MASTER_analysis.R
get_model_label <- function(x) {
  x_low <- tolower(x)
  case_when(
    grepl("gemini", x_low) ~ "Gemini",
    grepl("gpt", x_low) ~ "GPT",
    grepl("qwen|gwen", x_low) ~ "Qwen",
    TRUE ~ x
  )
}

level_to_group <- function(level) {
  case_when(
    level == "ARTICLE" ~ "Text",
    level == "ACTOR" ~ "Actor",
    level == "JUSTIF" ~ "Justification",
    level %in% c("ACT_REF", "ACTREF") ~ "Reference",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < .001) "p < 0.001" else paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", p))
}

# Proportions (0-1) -> percent (0-100); leaves data already on 0-100 untouched
to_percent <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(x)
  if (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1) x * 100 else x
}

complete_rows <- function(data, vars) {
  data |> filter(if_all(all_of(vars), ~ !is.na(.x)))
}

read_data <- function(file, reader) {
  path <- file.path(DATA_DIR, file)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop("Data file not found: ", normalizePath(path, mustWork = FALSE),
         ". Place it in the app folder or change DATA_DIR.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  reader(path)
}

model_order  <- c("Majority vote", "Gemini", "GPT", "Qwen")
group_levels <- c("Text", "Actor", "Justification", "Reference")

group_cols <- c(
  "Text" = "#2F2F2F",
  "Actor" = "#D55E00",
  "Justification" = "#0072B2",
  "Reference" = "#009E73"
)

# One key for the 17 variables: survey item stem, label, variable name in the
# reliability data, group. The order sets the order of the x-axis and the
# numbering 01-17 in the expert plot.
item_key <- tibble(
  item = c(
    "section", "pres", "tone", "opppos",
    "actrole", "actparty", "actorig", "actgen", "actrel",
    "justin", "justout", "justcg", "justrel",
    "actrefresp", "actrefval", "actrefrec", "actrefout"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Section", "Presentation", "Tone", "Opposing positions",
    "Actor role", "Actor party", "Actor origin", "Actor gender", "Actor religion",
    "Justification in-group", "Justification out-group",
    "Justification common good", "Justification religion",
    "Actor reference responsiveness", "Actor reference valence",
    "Actor reference recognition", "Actor reference outrage"
  ),
  variable_name = c(
    "SECTION", "FORM_OF_PRESENTATION", "TONE", "OPPOSING_POSITIONS",
    "ACT_ROLE_GENERAL", "ACT_PARTY_AFFILIATION", "ACT_ORIGIN", "ACT_GENDER",
    "ACT_RELIGIOUS_AFFILIATION",
    "JUST_IN_GROUP_REFERENCE", "JUST_OUT_GROUP_REF", "JUST_COMMON_GOOD_REF",
    "JUST_RELIGIOUS_BELIEFS_REF",
    "ACTREF_GENUINE_CONSTRUCTED_RESP_ACTOR", "ACTREF_VALENCE_ACTOR",
    "ACTREF_RECOGNITION_ACTOR", "ACTREF_OUTRAGE_ACTOR"
  ),
  group = c(
    rep("Text", 4), rep("Actor", 5), rep("Justification", 4), rep("Reference", 4)
  )
)
stopifnot(nrow(item_key) == N_ITEMS_EXPECTED)

# Construct names as in the article
dims <- c("know", "interpret", "clear", "complete")
dim_labels <- c(
  "know" = "Need for information",
  "interpret" = "Need for interpretation",
  "clear" = "Clarity of instructions",
  "complete" = "Completeness of instructions"
)
pred_labels <- setNames(dim_labels, paste0("M", names(dim_labels)))

# Outcomes (LLM-human reliability)
dv_info <- list(
  alpha = list(var = "LLM_Human_Kripp_Alpha", label = "Krippendorff's α",
               axis = "LLM–human Krippendorff's α", ref = ALPHA_REF,
               ref_text = "α = 0.60"),
  agree = list(var = "LLM_Human_Agreement", label = "Percentage agreement",
               axis = "LLM–human agreement (%)", ref = AGREE_REF,
               ref_text = "80% agreement")
)
dv_choices <- c("Krippendorff's α" = "alpha", "Percentage agreement" = "agree")


#############################################################
# 4. Data import and preparation
#############################################################

icr_list   <- read_data(FILE_ICR, readRDS)
human_icr  <- read_data(FILE_HUMAN_ICR, readRDS)
expert_raw <- read_data(FILE_EXPERT, readRDS)

# ---- Expert survey: mean, SD and 95% CI per variable and dimension ----
# The regex is anchored on the 17 item stems, so unrelated survey columns that
# happen to end in e.g. "complete" are never picked up.
expert_item_regex <- paste0(
  "^(", paste(item_key$item, collapse = "|"), ")(",
  paste(dims, collapse = "|"), ")$"
)

# One row per survey column (item x dimension)
expert_long <- bind_rows(lapply(
  grep(expert_item_regex, names(expert_raw), value = TRUE),
  function(col) {
    x <- as.numeric(expert_raw[[col]])
    n <- sum(!is.na(x))
    s <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(
      item = sub(expert_item_regex, "\\1", col),
      type = sub(expert_item_regex, "\\2", col),
      M = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = s,
      N = n,
      CI = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * s / sqrt(n)   # half-width of the 95% CI of the mean
    )
  }
))

# Wide: one row per item, columns Mknow, SDknow, Nknow, CIknow, Minterpret, ...
expert_summary <- item_key
for (d in dims) {
  part <- expert_long |> filter(type == d) |> select(item, M, SD, N, CI)
  names(part)[-1] <- paste0(names(part)[-1], d)
  expert_summary <- left_join(expert_summary, part, by = "item")
}

expert_summary <- expert_summary |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
    item = factor(item, levels = item_key$item)
  ) |>
  arrange(item) |>
  mutate(id_label = sprintf("%02d", row_number()))

stopifnot(nrow(expert_summary) == N_ITEMS_EXPECTED,
          !anyNA(expert_summary[paste0("M", dims)]))
n_experts <- max(expert_summary[paste0("N", dims)])

# ---- LLM-human reliability + human reliability + expert means ----
# Agreement is expressed on a 0-100 scale, as in the article.
prepare_reliability <- function(d) {
  d |>
    filter(!Level %in% EXCLUDED_LEVELS) |>
    left_join(human_icr, by = "Variable") |>
    left_join(expert_summary |> select(variable_name, label, group, starts_with("M")),
              by = c("Variable" = "variable_name")) |>
    rename(LLM_Human_Kripp_Alpha = Krippendorffs_Alpha,
           LLM_Human_Agreement = Agreement) |>
    mutate(
      LLM_Human_Agreement = to_percent(LLM_Human_Agreement),
      label = factor(label, levels = item_key$label)
    )
}

df_majority <- prepare_reliability(icr_list[["res_consensus"]])
df_indiv <- icr_list[["res_indiv"]] |>
  mutate(model_name = get_model_label(Comparison)) |>
  prepare_reliability()

# Datasets by model name; the server picks the one selected in the menu
analysis_sets <- list(
  "Majority vote" = df_majority,
  "Gemini" = df_indiv |> filter(model_name == "Gemini"),
  "GPT" = df_indiv |> filter(model_name == "GPT"),
  "Qwen" = df_indiv |> filter(model_name == "Qwen")
)
stopifnot(all(vapply(analysis_sets, nrow, integer(1)) == N_ITEMS_EXPECTED))

# Fixed y-axis ranges over all four models, so axes stay put when the model changes
range_all <- function(var) range(unlist(lapply(analysis_sets, `[[`, var)), na.rm = TRUE)


#############################################################
# 5. User interface (UI)
# Each tab: short introduction, figure, figure legend, menus below the figure,
# download buttons.
#############################################################

legend_style <- "font-size: 13px; color: #444; max-width: 900px;"

ui <- page_fluid(
  theme = app_theme,
  title = "The Text-Annotation Performance of LLMs",   # browser tab

  # Title above the tabs, stays on top when the tab changes
  div(
    style = "padding: 15px 20px 10px 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc; text-align: center;",
    div("The Text-Annotation Performance of LLMs Varies Across Levels of Task Complexity",
        style = "font-size: 22px; font-weight: bold;"),
    div("Interactive Figures for the Manuscript",
        style = "font-size: 14px; color: #34638B;")
  ),

  navset_tab(

    # ---- Tab 1: About ----
    nav_panel(
      "About",
      div(
        style = "max-width: 900px; padding-top: 15px;",
        h3("About this app"),
        p("Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to code texts in the social sciences, ",
          "but it is still unclear for which coding tasks they can replace human coders. ",
          "This app accompanies a study that asks how the complexity of a coding task shapes how well ",
          "LLM codes agree with a validated human-coding gold standard."),
        p("The study distinguishes two dimensions of coding-task complexity: ",
          strong("need for information"), ", the extent to which correct coding depends on knowledge ",
          "beyond the text itself, and ", strong("need for interpretation"), ", the extent to which ",
          "coding requires subjective judgment. Experts in content analysis rated 17 widely used coding ",
          "tasks on both dimensions. Three LLMs (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, GPT 5 Nano and Qwen3 235B) and ",
          "their majority vote then performed the same 17 coding tasks on 600 multilingual media texts from ",
          "newspapers, news websites and political blogs."),
        p("Across all models, coding tasks that need more interpretation are coded less reliably ",
          "(Krippendorff's α). Need for information shows no association on its own and at most a small ",
          "positive one when both dimensions are modeled jointly."),
        h4("How to use the app"),
        tags$ul(
          tags$li(strong("LLM Reliability: "),
                  "agreement between each model and the human gold standard for each of the 17 coding tasks."),
          tags$li(strong("Expert Survey: "),
                  "how the experts rated the coding tasks on need for information and need for ",
                  "interpretation, and on the clarity and completeness of the coding instructions."),
          tags$li(strong("Complexity and Reliability: "),
                  "regressions of LLM–human reliability on the expert ratings, for each model, ",
                  "with or without controls for the quality of the instructions.")
        ),
        p("Choose the measure, model or level of analysis in the menus below each figure. ",
          "Each figure and its data can be downloaded."),
        )
    ),

    # ---- Tab 2: LLM reliability per variable (bar chart) ----
    nav_panel(
      "LLM Reliability",
      p(style = "padding-top: 15px;",
        "Reliability between LLM coding and the human gold standard for each coding task."),
      plotOutput("llm_plot", height = PLOT_HEIGHT),
      div(style = legend_style, uiOutput("llm_legend")),
      hr(),
      layout_columns(
        selectInput("llm_measure", "Reliability measure:", choices = dv_choices),
        selectInput("llm_model", "Model:", choices = model_order)
      ),
      div(downloadButton("llm_png", "Figure (PNG)"),
          downloadButton("llm_csv", "Data (CSV)"))
    ),

    # ---- Tab 3: expert survey (two scatterplots) ----
    nav_panel(
      "Expert Survey",
      p(style = "padding-top: 15px;",
        "Mean expert ratings of the 17 coding tasks (1–5 scales)."),
      plotOutput("expert_plot", height = PLOT_HEIGHT),
      div(style = legend_style, uiOutput("expert_legend")),
      hr(),
      layout_columns(
        selectInput("survey_plot", "Dimensions:",
                    choices = c("Need for information vs. need for interpretation" = "complexity",
                                "Clarity vs. completeness of instructions" = "instructions")),
        selectInput("survey_group", "Level of analysis:", choices = c("All", group_levels))
      ),
      div(downloadButton("expert_png", "Figure (PNG)"),
          downloadButton("expert_csv", "Data (CSV)"))
    ),

    # ---- Tab 4: complexity and reliability (regressions) ----
    nav_panel(
      "Complexity and Reliability",
      p(style = "padding-top: 15px;",
        "Linear regressions of LLM–human reliability on the expert ratings (17 coding tasks)."),
      plotOutput("block_plot", height = PLOT_HEIGHT),
      div(style = legend_style, uiOutput("block_legend")),
      hr(),
      layout_columns(
        selectInput("uv", "Predictor:",
                    choices = c("Need for information" = "Mknow",
                                "Need for interpretation" = "Minterpret",
                                "Both (joint model)" = "both")),
        selectInput("cov", "Controls:",
                    choices = c("None" = "none",
                                "Clarity and completeness" = "both",
                                "Clarity" = "Mclear",
                                "Completeness" = "Mcomplete")),
        selectInput("dv", "Reliability measure:", choices = dv_choices),
        selectInput("model_b", "Model:", choices = model_order)
      ),
      div(downloadButton("block_png", "Figure (PNG)"),
          downloadButton("block_csv", "Data (CSV)"))
    )
  )
)


#############################################################
# 6. Server
# Each figure is built in a reactive(), so the plot output and the PNG
# download use the same object.
#############################################################

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # ===================================================================
  # LLM reliability: bar chart per variable, coloured by group, dashed
  # reference line, fixed y-axis across models
  # ===================================================================

  llm_data <- reactive({
    analysis_sets[[input$llm_model]] |>
      select(Level, Variable, label, group, LLM_Human_Kripp_Alpha, LLM_Human_Agreement)
  })

  llm_fig <- reactive({
    dv <- dv_info[[input$llm_measure]]
    lims <- if (input$llm_measure == "alpha") {
      c(min(-0.4, floor(range_all(dv$var)[1] * 10) / 10), 1)   # no bar is cut off
    } else {
      c(0, 100)
    }

    ggplot(llm_data(), aes(x = label, y = .data[[dv$var]], fill = group)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.75) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = dv$ref, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = lims) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = dv$axis) +
      theme_pnas() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            legend.position = "top")
  })

  output$llm_plot <- renderPlot(llm_fig())

  output$llm_legend <- renderUI({
    dv <- dv_info[[input$llm_measure]]
    model_text <- if (input$llm_model == "Majority vote") {
      "the majority vote of Gemini, GPT and Qwen"
    } else {
      input$llm_model
    }
    p(strong("LLM–human reliability per coding task. "),
      dv$label, " between the human gold standard and ", model_text, ". ",
      "Bars are coloured by level of analysis. The dashed line marks ", dv$ref_text, ". ",
      "N = 17 coding tasks.")
  })


  # ===================================================================
  # Expert survey: numbered points with 95% CI crosses, shaded quadrants,
  # number key on the right
  # ===================================================================

  expert_data <- reactive({
    d <- expert_summary
    if (input$survey_group != "All") d <- d |> filter(group == input$survey_group)
    d
  })

  expert_fig <- reactive({
    d <- expert_data()
    if (input$survey_plot == "complexity") {
      xd <- "know"; yd <- "interpret"
    } else {
      xd <- "clear"; yd <- "complete"
    }
    xvar <- paste0("M", xd); yvar <- paste0("M", yd)
    xci <- paste0("CI", xd); yci <- paste0("CI", yd)

    p_main <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[xvar]], y = .data[[yvar]])) +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 1, xmax = 3, ymin = 1, ymax = 3, fill = "grey97") +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 3, xmax = 5, ymin = 3, ymax = 5, fill = "grey94") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[yvar]] - .data[[yci]], ymax = .data[[yvar]] + .data[[yci]]),
                    width = 0, color = "grey65", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = .data[[xvar]] - .data[[xci]], xmax = .data[[xvar]] + .data[[xci]]),
                    orientation = "y", width = 0, color = "grey65", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_point(aes(fill = group), shape = 21, size = 7, color = "white", stroke = 0.3) +
      geom_text(aes(label = id_label), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, drop = FALSE) +
      coord_fixed(xlim = c(1, 5), ylim = c(1, 5)) +
      labs(x = paste0(dim_labels[[xd]], " (expert mean)"),
           y = paste0(dim_labels[[yd]], " (expert mean)")) +
      theme_pnas()

    # Key: number + variable label. The height is fixed to all 17 slots, so the
    # key does not stretch when a group is filtered.
    key <- d |> mutate(y = N_ITEMS_EXPECTED + 1 - as.integer(id_label))
    p_key <- ggplot(key, aes(y = y)) +
      geom_point(aes(x = 1, fill = group), shape = 21, size = 6, color = "white") +
      geom_text(aes(x = 1, label = id_label), color = "white", size = 2.6, fontface = "bold") +
      geom_text(aes(x = 1.15, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 3.6) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, drop = FALSE) +
      xlim(0.9, 3) +
      ylim(0.5, N_ITEMS_EXPECTED + 0.5) +
      theme_void() +
      theme(legend.position = "none")

    p_main + p_key + plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 1))
  })

  output$expert_plot <- renderPlot(expert_fig())

  output$expert_legend <- renderUI({
    dims_text <- if (input$survey_plot == "complexity") {
      "need for information and need for interpretation"
    } else {
      "clarity and completeness of the coding instructions"
    }
    group_text <- if (input$survey_group == "All") "" else
      paste0(" Only coding tasks at the ", input$survey_group, " level are shown.")
    p(strong("Expert ratings of the coding tasks. "),
      "Mean ratings of ", dims_text, " (1 = low, 5 = high) by N = ", n_experts,
      " experts in content analysis. Error bars show 95% CIs of the means. ",
      "Dashed lines mark the scale midpoint.", group_text)
  })


  # ===================================================================
  # Complexity and reliability
  # One predictor without controls -> scatterplot with regression line and
  # standardized beta (= r); otherwise -> standardized coefficients with 95% CIs
  # ===================================================================

  block_spec <- reactive({
    preds <- if (input$uv == "both") c("Mknow", "Minterpret") else input$uv
    covs <- switch(input$cov,
                   none = character(0),
                   both = c("Mclear", "Mcomplete"),
                   input$cov)
    list(dv = dv_info[[input$dv]], preds = preds, covs = covs,
         scatter = length(preds) == 1 && length(covs) == 0)
  })

  block_data <- reactive({
    s <- block_spec()
    analysis_sets[[input$model_b]] |>
      select(Variable, label, group, all_of(c(s$dv$var, s$preds, s$covs))) |>
      complete_rows(c(s$dv$var, s$preds, s$covs))
  })

  block_fig <- reactive({
    s <- block_spec()
    d <- block_data()

    # --- Case 1: scatterplot ---
    if (s$scatter) {
      xvar <- s$preds
      ct <- cor.test(d[[xvar]], d[[s$dv$var]])
      stat_text <- sprintf("β = %.2f, %s", ct$estimate, format_p(ct$p.value))
      y_scale <- if (input$dv == "agree") {
        scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"))
      } else {
        scale_y_continuous()
      }

      return(
        ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[xvar]], y = .data[[s$dv$var]])) +
          geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
                      color = "black", fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +
          geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.8, fill = "grey35", color = "black") +
          y_scale +
          coord_cartesian(xlim = range_all(xvar), ylim = range_all(s$dv$var)) +
          labs(x = paste0(pred_labels[[xvar]], " (expert mean)"), y = s$dv$axis,
               title = paste0(input$model_b, ": ", stat_text)) +
          theme_pnas() +
          theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
      )
    }

    # --- Case 2: coefficient plot (standardized, as in the article) ---
    vars <- c(s$dv$var, s$preds, s$covs)
    d_std <- d |> mutate(across(all_of(vars), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
    model <- lm(reformulate(c(s$preds, s$covs), response = s$dv$var), data = d_std)

    ci <- confint(model)
    coef_df <- tibble(
      term = names(coef(model)),
      estimate = unname(coef(model)),
      conf.low = ci[, 1],
      conf.high = ci[, 2]
    ) |>
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      mutate(term_label = factor(pred_labels[term], levels = rev(pred_labels[c(s$preds, s$covs)])))

    x_lim <- range(c(-1, 1, coef_df$conf.low, coef_df$conf.high))

    ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = estimate, y = term_label)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
      geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                    orientation = "y", width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, fill = "grey30", color = "black") +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = x_lim) +
      labs(x = "Standardized coefficient (β, 95% CI)", y = NULL,
           title = sprintf("%s: %s, R² = %.2f", input$model_b, s$dv$label,
                           summary(model)$r.squared)) +
      theme_pnas()
  })

  output$block_plot <- renderPlot(block_fig())

  output$block_legend <- renderUI({
    s <- block_spec()
    n <- nrow(block_data())
    if (s$scatter) {
      p(strong("Bivariate regression. "),
        s$dv$label, " between LLM (", input$model_b, ") and human coding, by the expert mean of ",
        tolower(pred_labels[[s$preds]]), ". The line shows the OLS fit with its 95% CI; ",
        "β is the standardized coefficient (equal to r). N = ", n, " coding tasks.")
    } else {
      ctrl_text <- if (length(s$covs) == 0) "" else
        paste0(", controlling for ", paste(tolower(pred_labels[s$covs]), collapse = " and "))
      p(strong("Multiple regression. "),
        "Standardized OLS coefficients with 95% CIs for ", s$dv$label,
        " between LLM (", input$model_b, ") and human coding",
        ctrl_text, ". Outcome and predictors are z-standardized. N = ", n, " coding tasks.")
    }
  })


  # ===================================================================
  # Downloads: figure as PNG (300 dpi) and the plotted data as CSV
  # ===================================================================

  png_handler <- function(name, fig, width = 9, height = 6) {
    downloadHandler(
      filename = function() paste0(name, ".png"),
      content = function(file) ggsave(file, fig(), width = width, height = height, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
    )
  }
  csv_handler <- function(name, data) {
    downloadHandler(
      filename = function() paste0(name, ".csv"),
      content = function(file) write.csv(data(), file, row.names = FALSE)
    )
  }

  output$llm_png    <- png_handler("llm_reliability", llm_fig)
  output$llm_csv    <- csv_handler("llm_reliability", llm_data)
  output$expert_png <- png_handler("expert_ratings", expert_fig, width = 10)
  output$expert_csv <- csv_handler("expert_ratings", expert_data)
  output$block_png  <- png_handler("complexity_reliability", block_fig, width = 7, height = 6)
  output$block_csv  <- csv_handler("complexity_reliability", block_data)
}


#############################################################
# Start app
#############################################################

shinyApp(ui, server)
